page: Microsoft Azure F64ams_v6 is a 64-vCPU virtual machine from the compute-optimized and memory-intensive Famsv6 series, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance assigns one dedicated physical thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Cache architecture consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported processor extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as cryptographic accelerators such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 512.0 GB, establishing a generous ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. In benchmark testing, the memory subsystem demonstrated 9,386.02 GB/sec in cached small-block reads, alongside large-block uncached read and write bandwidths of 301.02 GB/sec and 162.97 GB/sec, respectively. The instance includes no bundled local storage disks and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating network-attached storage such as Azure Premium Storage for operating system and application data.

Multi-core execution ranks in the top tier across several standardized benchmarks. Multi-threaded stress-ng produced a score of 196,948.17, while multi-core Geekbench reached 25,554.0 and PassMark CPU scored 92,281.36. The architecture also exhibited strong parallel processing efficiency in specialized tasks, achieving 72,890.0 in Clang software compilation, 99,655.0 in ray tracing, and 135.23 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. For machine learning inference, prompt processing reached 5,815.07 tokens per second on small models and 49.13 tokens per second for text generation on medium models.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio and lack of integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, the F64ams_v6 is structurally designed for memory-resident and compute-heavy enterprise tasks. Workloads that benefit most include in-memory databases, large-scale software build environments, scientific modeling, batch data compression, and CPU-driven model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F64ams_v6 is a compute-optimized and memory-intensive virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 512 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware capabilities include hardware virtualization and AVX-512 vector instructions with BF16 and VNNI support. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core computing power, highlighted by 196,948.17 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 72,890.0 in Clang software compilation, and 135.23 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, requiring external premium network storage for persistent disk IO. With its high memory density and dedicated core architecture, the F64ams_v6 delivers strong resource efficiency for memory-heavy databases, large parallel builds, scientific simulations, and CPU-based inference workloads.
